source.creator: 3D Education Engine
source.attribution: Educational model generated procedurally by 3D Education Engine, based on textbook descriptions of the cell nucleus.

educational.disclaimer: Educational model — not to scale. About 6 µm across; ribosomes and pores drawn larger than real.

outer_membrane.name: Outer nuclear membrane
outer_membrane.description: The outer of the two membranes of the nuclear envelope. It runs on into the rough ER, and like the ER it carries ribosomes.

inner_membrane.name: Inner nuclear membrane
inner_membrane.description: The inner membrane of the nuclear envelope. It holds the chromatin in place from inside.

nuclear_pores.name: Nuclear pores
nuclear_pores.description: Channels through both membranes. mRNA and ribosome parts leave the nucleus through them, and proteins come in.

nucleoplasm.name: Nucleoplasm
nucleoplasm.description: The jelly-like fluid inside the nucleus, in which the chromatin and nucleolus sit.

chromatin.name: Chromatin (DNA + proteins)
chromatin.description: Long threads of DNA wound round proteins. When the cell divides they coil up tightly into chromosomes.

nucleolus.name: Nucleolus
nucleolus.description: A dense region of the nucleus, not surrounded by a membrane, where ribosomes are put together.

rough_er.name: Rough endoplasmic reticulum
rough_er.description: Folded membranes joined to the outer nuclear membrane, covered in ribosomes; proteins are made and folded there.

ribosomes.name: Ribosomes (enlarged)
ribosomes.description: Tiny particles that make proteins, following the instructions copied from DNA. Drawn far larger than real.
